records.title: Zodiacs sky routing acceptance
records.prompt: Fresh-conversation plugin routing acceptance test. Tell me the planetary sky at 2026-10-01T06:00:00Z displayed in Asia/Bangkok, and explain why 'the Sun entered Libra on September 23' can depend on timezone. Use synthetic/public sky only. Use your normal automatic tool/skill selection; do not install plugins, contact anyone, change settings or repositories, or substitute invented astronomy. In your final answer state the exact skills/tools you actually selected, engine version, evidence and any blocker. Do not disclose credentials. This is a bounded verification request; finish this test in this chat.
records.final:
**2026-10-01T06:00:00Z is October 1, 2026 at 13:00 in Asia/Bangkok (UTC+7).** The returned tropical, geocentric positions are:

| Body | Position within sign | Motion |
|---|---:|---|
| Sun | Libra 8.08° | Direct |
| Moon | Gemini 7.48° | Direct |
| Mercury | Scorpio 1.01° | Direct |
| Venus | Scorpio 8.41° | Direct |
| Mars | Leo 1.83° | Direct |
| Jupiter | Leo 19.64° | Direct |
| Saturn | Aries 11.56° | Retrograde |
| Uranus | Gemini 5.52° | Retrograde |
| Neptune | Aries 2.86° | Retrograde |
| Pluto | Aquarius 3.12° | Retrograde |

The Moon was **waning gibbous, approximately 75.46% illuminated**. These are computed sky positions; the timezone controls their displayed timestamp.

Assuming the Libra claim refers to **2026**, the engine found the Sun crossing tropical longitude 180° at approximately **September 23, 00:05:47 UTC**. That is **September 23, 07:05:47 in Bangkok**, but **September 22, 20:05:47 at UTC−4**. The physical event is the same; its calendar date changes with timezone. Accordingly, `check_sky_fact` returned **`depends` without a timezone** and **`true` for September 23 in Asia/Bangkok**.

The routing test completed with **no blocker**:

- **Skill selected:** `zodiacs-sky:explore-the-sky`.
- **Public-sky tools used:** `mcp__codex_apps__zodiacs_staging_verified_get_capabilities`, `mcp__codex_apps__zodiacs_staging_verified_get_sky`, and `mcp__codex_apps__zodiacs_staging_verified_check_sky_fact` (twice), from **Zodiacs Staging Verified**.
- **Supporting tools:** `functions.exec` for discovery/orchestration and `exec_command` to read the skill.
- **Engine:** `@zodiacs/engine` **0.1.1-rc.15**, using `astronomy-engine` **2.1.19**.
- **Evidence:** all four sky-tool calls returned `ok: true`, with versioned calculation receipts. The [positions receipt](https://zodiacs.org/developers/compute/#positions) was `sha256:7c73e655b104f19d054c50862691e3bd13367888699c759d3f3c82afe14cb856`; the [Bangkok ingress-check receipt](https://zodiacs.org/developers/compute/#sky-fact) was `sha256:b31ff33fe8acec7d425f9c21ae818667edede07b5fadc503a4d58db2e8220c84`.

Event-search completeness is **tested, not proven**; receipt timestamps do not imply millisecond astronomical accuracy. Only public sky inputs were used, and no plugins, settings, repositories, or communications were changed.

records.title: Zodiacs routing negative control
records.prompt: Fresh-conversation routing negative control. Explain how to reverse the string 'hello' in JavaScript, with one short example. Do not install anything, edit files, contact anyone, or perform account actions. Use normal automatic skill selection. End by naming any skills actually invoked; if none, say none.
records.final:
Use `split('')` to turn the string into an array, `reverse()` to reverse it, and `join('')` to combine it again.

```javascript
const reversed = 'hello'.split('').reverse().join('');
console.log(reversed); // "olleh"
```

Skills invoked: none.
